narrative: Constructed 2026-08-29 as the worked example of the SIGNAL language (the wider shelf). A two-person operations agency that builds order systems and back-office automations for small manufacturers; they open with their three verbs (Map / Build / Hand over), speak in direct numbered steps, and have a logo they don't care about. Fills library holes: craft_first (the interview's hero verbs), practicing + curious audience, no_stance conventions, existing_disposable maturity, discrete_artifacts and high_conviction — the exact signal set the style interview emits most and no exemplar showed. Resulting direction: ONE GRID, ONE COLOUR — white ground, a 12-column grid you can feel, a flat blue that appears only on the current step, everything numbered, a mono for labels. Teaches: numbered-offer hero, modular blocks with 2px top rules, the mono label voice, proof stated as a flat count, and a single subtle entrance instead of ambient motion.

evidence: their three verbs: Map / Build / Hand over
step one, step two, step three
we don't do discovery calls; we do a map
plant managers and owners who already run a floor
who it's for, in their words: people drowning in spreadsheets who suspect there's a better way

palette.because: P4: a light room with daylight honesty for an overwhelmed operator; one flat blue marks the current step and the one button (P3) — no gradients, no washes.

typography.pairing_logic: A precise geometric sans at heavy weight for the numbered headlines; a mono for every label, step number and figure so the page reads like a well-kept spec sheet. Kinship in precision (P5, alongside), contrast in size.
typography.because: Direct, data-led speech → type that looks measured; the mono label voice is the agency's handwriting.

layout.because: Their offer is three discrete artifacts — three equal blocks with a 2px top rule each, numbered 01/02/03, on a 12-column grid whose gutters stay visible in the spacing.

motion.signature_move: the step that lights up — the current block's top rule turns blue as it enters
motion.because: P8: one move that restates 'you are here'; nothing else moves.

hero_concept.concept_statement: The three verbs stacked as a numbered list at display scale — 01 Map, 02 Build, 03 Hand over — with the current one in blue; beneath, one sentence of who it is for and a flat count of systems shipped.
hero_concept.because: craft_first → the verbs ARE the headline; proof as a count (P15) rather than a claim.

whitespace.because: P2: blocks sit on a visible rhythm with generous gutters; the page never fills space to prove effort.

notes: every 'step one / step two' in their copy becomes a mono label 01 / 02 / 03
the process module is the hero repeated at smaller scale — same rules, same numbers
the client list is a plain two-column text index, not logos
the contact block is a form with mono labels and one blue button
voice_to_visual.because: A numbered voice becomes a numbered page; labels do the work adjectives would.

rule_break.what: no photograph anywhere on the home page — the grid and the numbers carry it
rule_break.because: Agencies sell with photos of laptops; a page with none is the one deliberate refusal.

tension.pole_b: sitting on the floor with you
tension.expression: Precision owns the grid, the mono, the numbers; the alongside pole owns the second-person copy, the 'we come to you' line and the guide-shaped process module.
tension.because: Precision alone reads as a vendor; warmth alone reads as unqualified — they are both.

first_impression.feel_in_3s: These people are organised; I could hand them the mess.
first_impression.remember: The three numbered verbs with one lit in blue.
first_impression.because: legit_intentional for an overwhelmed operator = order visible before a word is read.

language.because: A systems business with three discrete artifacts, a direct numbered voice and bold conviction — one grid, one colour; Broadsheet would slow a reader who wants steps, Glass has no product screen to show.

distinctiveness_check.notes: Only light-cool page in the library; nearest is e6 (single accent, balanced, subtle entrance, typographic hero) but on a white ground with a geometric face and a mono voice none of them use; shares the grid with e3/e7 on the opposite ground.

summary_for_practitioner: Your site is one grid and one colour. Your three verbs are the headline, numbered 01, 02, 03, with the current one lit in blue; every label on the page is set in a small typewriter-style face so it reads like a well-kept spec sheet. There is no photograph on the home page — the order itself is the picture. Your process repeats the same numbered rules at a smaller size, your clients are a plain text index, and the only motion is the blue rule that lights up on the step you are reading.
